subject: Proof of Subprocessor Data Residency and UK Addendum Proxying
messages:
From: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@healthcore.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@healthcore.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Proof of subprocessor residency requirements for UK addendum

Lukas / team,

Quick one from our privacy team as we prepare the UK addendum signature: HealthCore needs a substantiated list of all downstream subprocessors that potentially process UK personal data (including cloud infra partners, telemetry/metrics vendors, and monitoring agents). Specifically we need:

- A CSV with subprocessor name, location (country/region), whether we have an SCC + UK Addendum in place, and whether Redwood asserts onshore processing for UK data (yes/no).
- For any subprocessors outside the UK/EU, a short note on technical/contractual mitigations (TIAs/DTIAs, encryption at rest, KV caching segregation, etc.)

Two clarifying questions while you prepare that: do you treat your cloud infra (e.g. infra-owned EC2/GPU pools) as Redwood subprocessors for the purposes of the UK Addendum, or as downstream subprocessors where HealthCore would require evidence from the cloud provider? Second, will Redwood accept acting as the "proxying" controller for the UK Addendum (i.e., Redwood signs for subprocessor chain assurances) or do we need each subprocessor to countersign?

We'd like to get the CSV by end of day Wednesday (2027-06-02) to keep the legal cadence. If easier, a 20-min call tomorrow morning to walk through is fine.

Thanks,
Matt O'Neill
Head of Privacy – HealthCore
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@healthcore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Proof of subprocessor residency requirements for UK addendum

Matt — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: Redwood will act as the primary signer of the UK Addendum and will provide a subprocessor residency matrix (CSV) that shows country-level processing and whether SCCs + UK Addendum coverage is present. For subprocessors outside the UK/EU we provide both contractual (SCCs + DTIA/TIA where applicable) and technical mitigations; we will note those in the CSV.

Regarding cloud infra: we classify hyperscaler providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) as infrastructure subprocessors. They are listed on our subprocessor registry and we include their region of processing. For the purposes of HealthCore's UK Addendum, we can assert (and will document) that customer-specific inference workloads for UK-scoped customers are routed to UK/EU regions by default and that we and the infra provider are bound by contractual safeguards. Where a customer requests strict onshore-only handling (UK-residency exception), we support onshore-only footprint or dedicated pools and will mark that in the CSV.

I've attached a short summary of our SCC/UK Addendum handshake and typical mitigations — this is high level but should help your legal team. We'll produce the full CSV by EOD Wednesday.

Attachment: redwood_scc_handshake_summary.pdf (1 page stub — high-level summary)

Would you like me to drop into a 20-min sync tomorrow at 09:00 BST?

— Lukas Meyer
Head of Account – Redwood Inference

Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Proof of subprocessor residency requirements for UK addendum

Matt — thanks for sending the CSV. I reviewed the flagged rows and here is the position from a contract/controls perspective:

- CloudOps Ltd: Redwood treats CloudOps as an infrastructure subprocessor. We maintain contractual flow-down (SCCs where applicable) and operational controls (region pinning, separate VPCs for dedicated pools, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys when requested). That means we can assert coverage for CloudOps as part of Redwood's subprocessor chain for HealthCore's UK Addendum — no vendor countersignature required in the general case. For your flagged logging pipeline specifically, we will provide evidence (logs location and retention) and a short statement confirming no automatic US egress for UK-scoped jobs.

- MetricsAIO: this vendor exposes a residency option but it is not enabled by default. For HealthCore we will either disable the vendor's cross-border fallback or move metrics to a vendor-hosted EU-only bucket. We will note the chosen config in the CSV and include a follow-up attestation.

Next steps: Lukas will upload an updated residency matrix to the Drive link below and we will provide a one-page attestation for CloudOps and MetricsAIO within 3 business days. After you confirm acceptance I will prepare the final UK Addendum signature package and DocuSign envelope.

Drive: https://drive.re.redwood/HC-4901/evidence
DocuSign plan: DOCUSIGN:abc123

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference
